title: SAF tree IDs map to primary storage without authority binding
description: After a document-tree selection, the native bridge maps a tree document ID with volume prefix primary to a shared-storage path without checking URI authority; it rejects .. but permits dot segments. The host accepts shared-storage paths, while the Linux runtime has a separate configured-root allowlist. Provider behavior and workspace reachability are unresolved.
claimed_root_cause: resolvePickedPath trusts a provider-supplied primary volume prefix without binding it to the URI authority or rejecting dot segments.

trace.description: The picker request reaches the native document-tree picker.
A primary volume ID is mapped to /storage/emulated/0/<relative path>.

evidence.description: The mapping rejects empty, absolute, and .. segments but allows dot segments.
The host picker accepts a shared-storage prefix and does not reject dot segments.
Runtime host binding is restricted to configured workspace/shared-directory roots.

blockers: Android provider behavior does not establish whether a third-party DocumentsProvider can return a relevant crafted primary document ID.
The pinned client picker is absent and it is unknown whether a mapped path can satisfy runtime host-path allowlists and become model-readable.
No isolated Android test provider or compliant execution sandbox was available.

validation_plan.local: On an isolated Android test device, use a purpose-built DocumentsProvider and dummy directories to record the returned authority/document ID and whether a dot-segment ID maps outside the selected node. Trace only the callback and configured workspace roots.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the Android owner verify supported provider behavior and the pinned picker/workspace configuration with a disposable test profile and dummy files.
